details: The overall cryptocurrency market capitalization saw a 1.1% increase, reaching $2.63 trillion. Bitcoin demonstrated a rebound, trading at $76,420 after experiencing a three-day decline. However, U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded net outflows of $138 million on April 29. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) also opted to maintain interest rates between 3.50% and 3.75%.
title: Bitcoin Rebounds to $76,420 Amid Market Cap Increase, Despite ETF Outflows

details: The United States Federal Reserve's recent decision to hold interest rates steady led to significant volatility in the crypto market, resulting in over $500 million in liquidations within a 24-hour period. Bitcoin's price stalled above the $76,000 mark following the announcement, indicating market sensitivity to macroeconomic policy.
title: Fed Decision Triggers Over $500 Million in Crypto Liquidations as Bitcoin Stalls

details: Patrick Witt, a digital asset adviser to the White House, confirmed that the Trump administration has successfully navigated a significant legal hurdle concerning the centralized custody of the government's substantial Bitcoin reserves. This development hints at a forthcoming landmark announcement regarding the U.S. strategic Bitcoin stockpile.
title: White House Teases Major Announcement on US Bitcoin Stockpile Custody

details: A new cryptocurrency address, identified as 0x448…aD525, has accumulated 40,000 ETH, valued at approximately $90.64 million, through two transactions from FalconX. This significant accumulation has prompted speculation among analysts, suggesting a possible connection to Bitmine.
title: New Address Accumulates 40,000 ETH, Potentially Linked to Bitmine

details: Robinhood's crypto revenue and trading volume experienced a substantial decline, plummeting by nearly 50% after the platform missed its first-quarter earnings expectations. This downturn could indicate a reduction in retail investor activity within the cryptocurrency market.
title: Robinhood Crypto Revenue and Volume Plunge Nearly 50% in Q1
